docs.text: Binderdash ¶ Binderdash filters, ranks, and designs DNA constructs for de novo protein binders. Point it at the output folders from your design runs to inspect scores and structures in one interface, filter and rank candidates, and export ready-to-order DNA constructs. Features ¶ Reads run output folders directly from RFdiffusion, RFdiffusion3, BindCraft, and BoltzGen, and detects nf-binder-design pipeline outputs without reformatting. Displays designs from different runs and methods in one sortable table, matching common metrics (ipTM, interface PAE, RMSD, pLDDT) across pipelines that name them differently. Includes a Mol* 3D structure viewer to step through designs, colour by chain or pLDDT, overlay a reference structure, and mark designs as good or bad. Filters and ranks designs using score thresholds and target-contact conditions (for example, binding within 5 Å of selected epitope residues), multi-metric ranking, and diversity-aware shortlisting. The filter cascade UI shows how many designs each condition removes. See Filtering and ranking . Plots scatterplots and histograms for any pair of metrics. Saves design shortlists together with the filters and ranking that produced them. Designs DNA constructs with N- or C-terminal affinity tags and linkers (His, FLAG, Strep-tag II, AviTag, and others), codon optimisation under synthesis complexity constraints (GC content, hairpins, restriction sites), vendor-compatible short names, and Twist-ready CSV export. Exports design bundles containing structures, sequences, tables, selections, filters, and settings so a shortlist can be traced and restored later. Merges extra columns from uploaded TSV files (for example, lab results) onto designs by ID for filtering and ranking. Runs as a local desktop app or a shared server with sign-in (local accounts, Unix/PAM, or Google), per-user API keys, and an optional MCP endpoint and REST API for AI agents. Getting started ¶ Desktop app : download a build for Linux, macOS, or Windows from the latest release for local single-user use. Server with Docker : host a shared instance for a group, with HTTPS and sign-in . docs.text: Backup and restore ¶ Binderdash stores server state in a SQLite database, your run output directories, and configuration files. For full details on each storage location, see Storage architecture . Files to back up ¶ Component Docker Compose path Non-Docker server path Back up SQLite database ./data/binderdash.sqlite on the host ( /app/data in the container) The path in DATABASE , or backend/data/binderdash.sqlite if DATABASE is unset Yes, essential Run output directories The host directories mounted into the container and listed in RUN_BASE_DIRS The directories in RUN_BASE_DIRS Yes , if not already covered by your storage backups .env ./.env ./.env Yes (contains secrets, store it securely) docker-compose.yml , Caddyfile Repository root - Yes, if you have edited them Caddy TLS certificates caddy_data Docker volume - Optional Other server files do not need backups: bundle downloads are created in a temporary spool directory and deleted after transfer, and the built frontend is packaged in the container image. Database ¶ Some data exists only in the database and cannot be reconstructed from run folders: Saved Sets and their frozen design lists. Per-design annotations made in the UI or via the API/MCP ( tag and good flags, short names, edited sequences and binder chains, and columns merged from extra TSV/CSV files). Users, login identities, and API keys (keys are stored as SHA-256 hashes, so clients must create new keys if this table is lost). The database also stores ingested run and design rows along with cached metrics (tag placement, structural metrics, and target contacts). You can rebuild those tables by re-scanning and re-ingesting the runs, though recomputing metrics is slow on large installations and does not recover the annotations above. The backup contains user email addresses, so store it with the same access controls as .env . Run output directories ¶ Binderdash opens run folders read-only and does not modify them. Because these directories are usually large and managed by your pipeline storage, they may already have separate backups. When restoring them: Restore runs to their original paths. The database records absolute paths into these directories; if the paths change, design rows remain visible, but Mol* viewing and structure downloads fail. Restore the directories (and their Docker volume mounts) before starting Binderdash. Run files are served only from inside RUN_BASE_DIRS , and startup fails if any RUN_BASE_DIRS directory is missing. .env ¶ .env defines SECRET_KEY , LOCAL_USERS password hashes, the Google OAuth client secret, BINDERDASH_ADMIN_USERS , DATABASE , and RUN_BASE_DIRS . If SECRET_KEY changes, active browser sessions and outstanding download links become invalid and users must log in again. Stored data and API keys are unaffected. When SECRET_KEY is unset, Binderdash generates a random key on startup, invalidating existing sessions on restart. Set SECRET_KEY explicitly in production. Caddy certificates ¶ The caddy_data volume stores the TLS certificates obtained by Caddy. Backing it up is optional because Caddy requests new certificates automatically if the volume is missing, though keeping the volume avoids certificate authority rate limits during repeated rebuilds. Desktop app ¶ The desktop app stores its database, settings ( desktop.json ), and log in a per-user directory: Linux: ~/.local/share/binderdash/ (or $XDG_DATA_HOME/binderdash/ ) macOS: ~/Library/Application Support/Binderdash/ Windows: %LOCALAPPDATA%\Binderdash\ Back up binderdash.sqlite (plus -wal if present, see below) and desktop.json . Browser-local state ¶ Table layouts, column choices, unsaved filter settings, and similar UI state are stored in each user's browser (IndexedDB). Server backups do not include this state, and restoring a server does not affect it. Taking a database backup ¶ SQLite runs in WAL mode, so recent writes may still be in binderdash.sqlite-wal instead of the main database file. Do not copy binderdash.sqlite directly while the server is running : the copy can miss recent writes or become inconsistent. Online backup (service running) ¶ SQLite's online backup API writes a consistent snapshot without stopping Binderdash. The container image does not include the sqlite3 CLI, so use Python's sqlite3 module: docker compose exec binderdash python -c \ "import sqlite3,sys; sqlite3.connect(sys.argv[1]).backup(sqlite3.connect(sys.argv[2]))" \ /app/data/binderdash.sqlite /app/data/binderdash-backup.sqlite This writes ./data/binderdash-backup.sqlite on the host. Move it out of ./data to your off-host backup storage. If you run Binderdash directly on a host, or have the sqlite3 CLI installed on the Docker host: sqlite3 data/binderdash.sqlite ".backup /path/to/backups/binderdash-$(date +%F).sqlite" Both commands are safe to schedule with cron. Offline backup (service stopped) ¶ Stop the service ( docker compose stop binderdash ), then copy binderdash.sqlite and, if present, binderdash.sqlite-wal . You do not need to copy the -shm file. Verifying a backup ¶ python3 -c "import sqlite3,sys; print(sqlite3.connect(sys.argv[1]).execute('PRAGMA integrity_check').fetchone()[0])" \ binderdash-backup.sqlite This prints ok when the database passes SQLite's integrity check. Restoring ¶ Stop the service with docker compose stop binderdash (or stop the server process). If .env or the run directories were lost, restore them to their original paths. Delete any leftover -wal and -shm files before replacing the database file. Applying a stale WAL file from the previous database to a restored snapshot can corrupt the database. rm -f data/binderdash.sqlite-wal data/binderdash.sqlite-shm cp /path/to/backups/binderdash-2026-11-20.sqlite data/binderdash.sqlite Check file ownership: under Docker Compose, BINDERDASH_UID:BINDERDASH_GID must have write permission (see Docker deployment ). Start the service with docker compose start binderdash . At startup, Binderdash loads all runs and designs from the database into memory, making restored data immediately available. Backups from older Binderdash versions are upgraded automatically on startup (see Database migrations ). Restoring a backup from a newer Binderdash version onto an older version is not supported.

docs.text: Database migrations ¶ Summary ¶ Schema migrations run automatically whenever Binderdash opens the database, including server startup and python -m backend.cli commands. Migrations are strictly additive (new tables, new columns, or rows backfilled from older tables); no migration drops or renames tables or columns. Downgrades are not supported. To roll back an upgrade, restore your pre-upgrade backup. Migration mechanism ¶ Binderdash does not use a migration framework or a schema version number. When create_repository() in backend/persistence/factory.py creates the SQLite repository, it calls init_schema() in backend/persistence/sqlite_repo.py , which: Creates missing tables and indexes with CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS and CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS . New tables in a release are added here. Calls each _migrate_* method in order, inspecting the current schema ( PRAGMA table_info , sqlite_master ) and applying changes only when missing: _migrate_binder_chain_column , _migrate_short_name_column , _migrate_extra_data_column : add columns to binderdash_designs . _migrate_run_path_column , _migrate_ingested_at_column : add columns to binderdash_runs . _migrate_auth_users_to_user_model : copies logins from the legacy binderdash_auth_users table into binderdash_users and binderdash_user_identities , leaving existing identities untouched and keeping the legacy table in place. Each step is idempotent: up-to-date databases are unchanged, and an interrupted startup completes the remaining steps on the next launch. Migrations do not emit log output. Only the sqlite scheme is supported in DATABASE (Postgres is not implemented). Configuring any other scheme causes startup to fail with an error. Upgrading a server ¶ Take a backup (see Backup and restore ). Update the code and rebuild: git pull docker compose build --build-arg GIT_COMMIT=$(git rev-parse --short=12 HEAD) Restart with docker compose up -d . The new container upgrades the schema on startup. Check docker compose logs binderdash for errors and confirm /health responds. To roll back, stop the service, check out and rebuild the previous version, and restore your pre-upgrade backup. Running older code with a newer schema is untested. Running migrations manually ¶ Normal upgrades do not require manual steps. You can trigger migrations before starting the web server, for example to verify an upgrade on a copy of a production database. CLI commands open the database through the same DATABASE resolution and init_schema() path as the server, so a read-only command such as user list applies pending migrations and exits: # Non-Docker server, from the repository root with the venv active python -m backend.cli user list # Docker Compose, using the newly built image and the same ./data volume docker compose run --rm binderdash python -m backend.cli user list To test on a database copy instead of the live file, override DATABASE for the command: DATABASE="sqlite:////tmp/binderdash-copy.sqlite" python -m backend.cli user list Adding a migration (developers) ¶ Add a _migrate_* method to SqliteDesignsRepository and call it from init_schema() after the existing migration calls. Check the current schema first and return early if the change is already present, since init_schema() runs at startup. Keep migrations additive: do not drop or rename tables or columns, because installations may restore older backups and upgrade from earlier schemas. For new tables, add a CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS statement to the executescript block.

docs.text:
REST API ¶ Binderdash exposes a FastAPI REST API used by the Vue frontend and by scripts that analyse binder design runs. The same service also serves the built SPA and static assets. Pipeline outputs (BindCraft, RFdiffusion, RFdiffusion3, BoltzGen, and others recognised by run signatures ) are ingested into SQLite (or Postgres), cached in memory, and returned as JSON. Design rows include every column from the upstream results table plus Binderdash metadata. For machine-readable schemas, use the live OpenAPI document on your deployment. This page describes behaviour, authentication, and typical workflows. Base URL and OpenAPI ¶ Environment Typical base URL Your deployment https://binderdash.example.com Docker dev ( docker-compose.dev.yml ) http://localhost:8911 (host port mapped to container 8000 ) Local uvicorn http://localhost:8000 Resource Path Swagger UI /docs ReDoc /redoc OpenAPI JSON /openapi.json Health (no auth) /health (returns {"status": "healthy", "timestamp": "..."} ) Treat /openapi.json as authoritative for request and response shapes. The examples below cover common cases; new fields or routes may appear only in the spec. Authentication ¶ Protected routes require credentials unless DISABLE_AUTHENTICATION=true (all endpoints public). Discover what is enabled: GET /api/auth/status Response includes auth_disabled and providers ( local , pam , google ) plus a top-level api_keys: {enabled, reason} ( reason is null , "auth_disabled" , or "persistence_disabled" ). Configure auth via .env (see .env.example ). Relevant variables: Variable Purpose DISABLE_AUTHENTICATION When true , skip all auth and CSRF checks LOCAL_USERS user:bcrypt_hash,... for POST /api/auth/login PAM_LOCAL_* Optional Unix PAM after local users PAM_GECOS_EMAIL When true , resolve a PAM user's email from the GECOS "other" (5th) field only GOOGLE_AUTH_* Optional Google OAuth SECRET_KEY JWT signing for session cookies BINDERDASH_ADMIN_USERS Comma-separated allowlist (email, provider:identifier , or bare username) granting admin; re-applied at every startup and login DATABASE Required for per-user API keys (stored in the database) API key (scripts and automation) ¶ API keys are per-user, named, expiring, and revocable ; there is no single shared server secret. Create one in the web UI (account menu, top-right > "API keys") or via CLI: python -m backend.cli user create --email you@example.org --admin python -m backend.cli key create you@example.org --name bootstrap The token is printed to stdout (a warning goes to stderr) and shown once: the server stores a SHA-256 hash instead of plaintext. Keys require DATABASE ; without persistence, key endpoints return 503 . Once you have a token, send it on every request, including POST / PATCH / DELETE . No session cookie or CSRF header is required. Supported headers (either is fine): Authorization: Bearer <token> X-Binderdash-Api-Key: <token> export BINDERDASH_TOKEN='<token from `key create`>' export BASE='https://binderdash.example.com' curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $BINDERDASH_TOKEN" "$BASE/api/runs" GET /api/auth/status reports api_keys.enabled: true when keys are usable (auth is enabled and DATABASE is configured). Invalid, expired, or missing keys receive 401 Authentication required . Manage keys via GET/POST /api/api-keys and PATCH/DELETE /api/api-keys/{id} using a browser session only. API-key requests to those routes receive 403 so a leaked key cannot create its own replacement. GET /api/users is admin-only and session-only. Do not commit keys to the repository. Browser session (SPA) ¶ For interactive login (also required to create or manage API keys): POST /api/auth/login : body {"username": "...", "password": "..."} . Sets an HTTP-only session cookie and returns csrf_token and user . CSRF: state-changing methods ( POST , PUT , PATCH , DELETE ) must send header X-CSRF-Token matching the binderdash_csrf cookie. GET , HEAD , and OPTIONS are exempt. Missing or mismatched tokens return 403 with plain text CSRF token missing or CSRF token mismatch . POST /api/auth/logout : clears session and CSRF cookies. Google OAuth: GET /api/auth/google/login and GET /api/auth/google/callback (browser redirect flow). GET /api/auth/me returns the current user and requires a session cookie (API keys are not accepted; see backend/auth.py ). It returns username , provider , email , display_name , picture_url , user_id , is_admin , auth_method , and last_login_at . The login response ( POST /api/auth/login , and the Google callback) returns the same shape under user . User model ¶ A user is a person; an identity is one login method, (provider, identifier) (for example, local:alice , google:alice@example.org , pam:alice ). Identities merge onto the same user only when they share a verified email , and users are created automatically on first login. BINDERDASH_ADMIN_USERS (comma-separated; matches email, provider:identifier , or bare username, with no * wildcard) grants is_admin and is re-applied at every startup and login, so admin status set only via the CLI ( user set-admin ) is overwritten unless the user is also listed there. Data model ¶ There is no separate “project” resource. Entities relate as follows: flowchart LR Project["project_id
(from path)"] Run["Run
run_id UUID"] Design["Design
flat JSON row"] Project --> Run Run --> Design Project ¶ Logical grouping identified by project_id , inferred from directory structure when runs are scanned. List projects by grouping GET /api/runs results on project_id . Run ¶ One pipeline execution. Key fields: Field Description run_id Stable UUID (assigned at ingest) project_id Project name method bindcraft , bindcraft2 , rfd , rfd3 , rfd4_proteina , boltzgen , … path Filesystem path at ingest metadata.name Display name metadata.pdb_count Structure file count metadata.trajectory_count Trajectory / design count where available metadata.primary_score_stats Summary stats for the method’s primary score column metadata.merged_count Present when multiple paths merged under one name Runs with the same project_id and metadata.name may be merged; see merged_paths in stored run JSON. Design ¶ One row from the run’s results table, plus Binderdash fields. Each design is a flat JSON object : all upstream table columns are copied in, so column names depend on the pipeline (e.g. BindCraft Average_i_pTM , RFD3 iptm , rf3_ipsae_min ). Common Binderdash fields: Field Description design_id Primary identifier from results table backbone_id design_id with MPNN / AF2 / BindCraft2 _candidate{n} and _seq{n} suffixes removed run_id , project_id , run_name , method , run_path Run context pdb_file Structure basename (not full path) source_path Distinguishes rows when runs are merged good User flag (boolean) tag "N" or "C" : terminus receiving preset tags in Prepare Sequences Sequence Binder amino-acid sequence (stored in extra_data ; extract / tag-placement) binder_chain Chain ID used for sequence extract (default B ) short_name Twist / vendor short identifier (≤32 chars) Persistence: Pipeline columns from the on-disk results table are stored in data_json and replaced on re-ingest. User annotations (uploaded table columns, extracted sequence, plugins) are stored in extra_data and preserved across re-ingest. The API returns a single flat dict: {**data_json, **extra_data} plus dedicated columns. The in-memory designs list is sorted by each method’s primary score (see table below). Client-side filtering and re-sorting are normal. Method Primary score columns (first match used) Default sort in cache bindcraft Average_i_pTM ascending rfd pae_interaction ascending boltzgen design_to_target_iptm descending rfd3 iptm , pair_pae , rf3_ipsae_min , rf3_rmsd_target_aligned_binder_rmsd_all descending rfd4_proteina oracle_ppi_iptm_coi , else consensus_z (refolded runs only) descending bindcraft2 i_pDAE (absent for a design with no interface contacts; those sort last) descending RFD4-Proteina's combined_scores.tsv carries only identity and sequence. Its scores are merged on ingest from the oracle's sibling table ( of3_inline_metrics.csv for OpenFold3, af3_inline_metrics.csv for AlphaFold3) in the same directory, joined per batch - example_id repeats across batches, so the key is the batch from dataset_name plus example_id . Merged columns have their dots flattened to underscores ( oracle_ppi.iptm_coi becomes oracle_ppi_iptm_coi ), generation hyperparameters and work-directory paths are dropped, and inline_metrics_oracle records which oracle produced them. The oracle reports pTM, ipTM and pLDDT on 0-100; these are rescaled to 0-1 on merge so they match every other method, while the PAE and RMSD columns stay in angstroms. _coi means the chain of interest, which for a binder run is the binder chain. BindCraft2 publishes structures per stage: accepted designs ( ranked.csv ) in results/bc2/ranked/ , refolded candidates ( refolded.csv ) in each batch's 2_Refolded/Complexes/ . A run detected on ranked.csv lists both, so pdb_count can exceed the design count. Note also that BindCraft2's bare pLDDT column is the binder chain's , not the complex average ( Target_pLDDT and Unbound_Binder_pLDDT are separate), which is what canonical binder_plddt resolves to. For BindCraft, ascending Average_i_pTM means lower values sort first in the API cache; re-sort client-side if “higher is better” for your analysis. Export CSV with @csv instead of @tsv . Download one structure ¶ run_id="..." filename="design_model.cif" # from design.pdb_file curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $BINDERDASH_TOKEN" \ -o "${filename}" \ "$BASE/api/runs/${run_id}/files/structure/$(python3 -c "import urllib.parse; print(urllib.parse.quote('$filename'))")" Bulk download structures as tar ¶ items=$(curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $BINDERDASH_TOKEN" \ "$BASE/api/designs?run_ids=$runs" \ | jq '[.designs[] | select(.good==true) | {run_id, filename: .pdb_file}]') curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $BINDERDASH_TOKEN" \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -X POST "$BASE/api/pdbs/tar" \ -d "$(jq -n --argjson items "$items" '{items:$items}')" \ -o designs.tar DNA codon optimisation ¶ POST /api/sequences/optimize-dna back-translates and optimises protein sequences using DnaChisel and python_codon_tables . Request body: { "sequences": { "design_id_1": "MAEK...", "design_id_2": "MGSS..." }, "codon_table_id": "e_coli_316407", "method": "match_codon_usage", "constraints": [ { "type": "EnforceGCContent", "enabled": true, "params": { "mini": 0.25, "maxi": 0.64 } } ], "fixed": { "design_id_1": [false, false, false, true] }, "frame": { "design_id_1": 0 } } Optional fixed maps each design_id to a per-residue boolean array the same length as that protein. Residues marked true must be stops ( * , frozen as TAA ) or a leading Met ( M , frozen as ATG ), and are excluded from codon optimisation and from user constraints. When a design id is omitted from fixed (or fixed is omitted entirely), every * in that protein is treated as fixed. Each result row includes the seed that produced its DNA, and the response includes tool_versions (DnaChisel, python_codon_tables, numpy). Passing those seeds back as seeds: { design_id: 12345 } reproduces the same DNA while package versions match (a DnaChisel upgrade can change the search order for a given seed). Omitting seeds assigns a new random seed per design, allowing retries to succeed when a strict constraint set fails. Lowercase a / c / g / t in a sequence are literal nucleotides from a custom addition, not amino acids: they stay frozen and are not recoded. Optional frame maps each design_id to 0 , 1 or 2 , the nucleotide offset where design and preset-tag codons begin. A 5' addition with a length not divisible by 3 sets this to 1 or 2. AvoidConsecutiveCodons reads codons from that offset. Preparing constructs ¶ POST /api/sequences/prepare builds constructs (N/C tags, linkers, terminal prefixes and suffixes, start methionine, stop codons, post-stop padding, vendor short names, and protein parameters) from a design selection and a settings payload, returning the prepared rows and per-row warnings. The settings payload uses the same JSON format stored in a Prepare Sequences download bundle, so a saved bundle can be replayed. An invalid payload returns validation_errors instead of rows. POST /api/sequences/prepare/script returns a standalone Python script ( text/x-python ) that reproduces those constructs offline. The server generates it by inlining backend/seq_prep/ alongside a CONFIG block containing your settings, keeping the script matched to the server version. The script runs under uv run via a PEP 723 header, reads a TSV of designs with a tag column, outputs Twist CSV by default ( --format for FASTA/TSV/CSV/JSON), and embeds no sequences, hashes, or seeds so you can reuse it on later sets. This endpoint uses POST because the settings payload is a full JSON document. Codon tables ¶ GET /api/sequences/codon-tables returns { "items": [ { "value", "label" }, ... ] } . GET /api/sequences/codon-tables/{table_id} returns value , label , stop_codons , and codons_by_aa (mapping amino acid to codon to frequency). Common codon_table_id values: ID Organism e_coli_316407 E. coli K-12 (default in UI) s_cerevisiae_4932 S. cerevisiae h_sapiens_9606 Human c_griseus_10029 CHO ( C. griseus ) p_pastoris_4922 P. pastoris Optimisation method ¶ Passed to DnaChisel CodonOptimize : Value Behaviour match_codon_usage Match host codon usage (recommended) use_best_codon Highest-frequency codon per AA (can conflict with k-mer uniqueness) harmonize_rca Preserve relative adaptiveness when changing hosts Constraints ¶ Each constraint: { "type": "<name>", "enabled": true, "params": { ... } } . Type Parameters EnforceGCContent mini , maxi (0–1); optional window for local GC AvoidHairpins stem_size , hairpin_window (exact Watson-Crick stems only) AvoidPattern pattern : literal string, RepeatedKmerPattern , or "EnzymeName_site" (e.g. "BsaI_site" ) AvoidRareCodons min_frequency ; species injected from codon_table_id UniquifyAllKmers k (e.g. 12) AvoidInvertedRepeats min_tm (°C, default 68); optional stride (default 10) AvoidConsecutiveCodons codons (default CGG , CGA , CCC ), max_run (default 2). Runs are counted in the design/tag frame ( frame on the request), not from nucleotide 0 EnforceTranslation is always applied by the server; do not send it. The Prepare Sequences UI uses DEFAULT_TWIST_CONSTRAINTS in frontend/src/stores/seqPrep.ts , similar to the DNA optimisation/complexity rules used by Twist Biosciences for gene synthesis. The UI-only type ExcludeRestrictionSite with params.enzyme is serialised to AvoidPattern with pattern: "<enzyme>_site" before POST. AvoidInvertedRepeats rejects sequences with self-complementary structures (snapback hairpins) melting at or above min_tm , computed the same way primer3 and IDT do (concentration-free nearest-neighbour thermodynamic alignment). This detects the short GC-rich and imperfect inverted repeats that gene-synthesis vendors flag and that AvoidHairpins (exact stems only) misses. primer3's alignment scores at most 60 bp per sequence, so hairpins are scored on sliding 60 bp windows; structures spanning more than ~50 nt (long arms and loop) may not be detected. Optimisation response ¶ { "results": [ { "design_id": "d1", "optimized_dna": "ATG...", "error": null, "seed": 847392011 }, { "design_id": "d2", "optimized_dna": null, "error": "Constraints could not be resolved (No solution found).", "seed": null } ], "elapsed_seconds": 2.31, "tool_versions": { "dnachisel": "3.2.16", "numpy": "2.3.2", "python_codon_tables": "0.1.18" } } Failures are reported per design. Because DnaChisel's constraint search is stochastic, any design failing with "No solution found" is retried from the same starting sequence up to five times with a new seed each time before returning that error; the reported seed is from the succeeding attempt. All other errors return immediately. If many rows still fail, relax UniquifyAllKmers or windowed EnforceGCContent first. Sequence tags ¶ Preset tag amino-acid sequences are not stored as DNA on the server. The API stores only which terminus is active ( tag : "N" or "C" ); GET /api/sequences/tag-presets returns the preset table itself. Construct assembly is implemented in two places: in backend/seq_prep/ behind POST /api/sequences/prepare , and in TypeScript in frontend/src/stores/seqPrep.ts for the Prepare Sequences tab's live preview. Parity between them is verified by backend/tests/test_seq_prep_parity.py . Removing the TypeScript implementation is planned. Preset sequences ¶ Preset Sequence Terminus His-N HHHHHHSG N only His-C GSHHHHHH C only FLAG DYKDDDDK N or C cMyc EQKLISEEDL N or C HA YPYDVPDYA N or C AviTag GLNDIFEAQKIEWHE N or C Strep-tag II WSHPQFEK N or C C-tag EPEA C only SNAC-tag GSHHW (cleaved G↓SHHW ) N or C TEV-site ENLYFQS (cleaved ENLYFQ↓S ) N or C G4S linker GGGGS N or C STOP* * N or C Assembly order ¶ For binder sequence core (from Sequence , trailing * removed) and tag : [N-terminal prefix] [N-terminal tags if tag=="N"] core [C-terminal tags if tag=="C"] [C-terminal suffix] [optional *] Workflow for a C-terminal His tag: Ensure Sequence is set ( POST /api/designs/sequences if missing). PATCH /api/designs/tag with "tag": "C" . Build prepared_aa = core + "GSHHHHHH" + ("*" if including stop) . POST /api/sequences/optimize-dna with sequences: { design_id: prepared_aa } . Stops ( * ) are frozen as TAA; pass an optional fixed boolean array per design to mark which residues stay fixed. Use POST /api/designs/tag-placement to let the server choose N vs C from structure SASA and contacts. Further UI behaviour (post-stop padding, short names, mixed-case sequences) is documented in Sequence preparation . Filtering, ranking, and diversity selection ¶ Run scope for every /api/filtering/* call is an explicit run_ids list; there is no server-side "currently selected" state. How the Filtering tab uses these stages, including the BoltzGen-style weighted ranking, is described in Filtering and ranking . The pipeline has three independent stages, each individually reachable: Hard filters ( FilterSpec ): { "column": "...", "operator": "...", "threshold": <number|null>, "text_value": <string|null> } . column accepts a canonical metric name (see backend/filtering/metrics.py , e.g. iptm , rmsd , pae_interaction ) resolved per-method, a raw column name, one of the identity columns design_id / project_id / run_name / method / Sequence , or the user columns good and tag . Numeric operators < , <= , > , >= take threshold ; string operators contains , not_contains , starts_with , ends_with , equals , not_equals , regex take text_value ; is_empty / is_not_empty take neither. good is a three-state rating: equals with text_value "true" (good) or "false" (bad), or is_empty (unrated). tag is text ( N / C , or empty). Both columns are listed even when no design has a value yet; a missing column is treated as all null. Ranking ( RankingMetric ): { "column": "...", "weight": 1.0, "higher_is_better": true } , plus ranking_mode . worst_rank (the default when omitted, keeping older clients on boltzgen Algorithm 2) scales each design's rank on every metric by 1/weight and takes the worst (max) scaled rank. simple sorts lexicographically: more filters passed first, then the metrics in list order, ignoring weight . In both modes, num_filters_passed is included in the sort and failing designs are not dropped ; ranked always covers every input design. The Filtering tab sends simple by default. Diversity selection ( select_diverse ): lazy-greedy selection over binder sequence similarity + quality_score , controlled by budget (final set size), alpha (0 = quality only, 1 = diversity only), and optional size_buckets ( {"min", "max", "num_designs"} , capping selections per sequence-length range). Only designs that passed every hard filter are eligible : a design failing a filter cannot appear in the diverse or saved set, regardless of how small passing_filters is relative to budget . best_mpnn_only (default false) first keeps one design per backbone_id (best primary score; designs with no backbone are kept) so the budget is not spent on MPNN variants of the same backbone. It applies only when diversity selection runs. POST /api/filtering/run accepts a FilteringRunRequest body: name , run_ids , filters , metrics , budget (default 24), alpha (default 0, quality only; BoltzGen uses 0.001 for proteins and 0.01 for its peptide-anything protocol), size_buckets , random_state , apply_diversity (default true; when false, the saved set includes every design that passed the hard filters and budget / alpha are ignored for selection), and best_mpnn_only (default false; see stage 3). POST /api/filtering/diversity accepts the same selection fields without persisting a set. Response: { "saved_set_id": "...", "name": "...", "total_input": 10000, "passing_filters": 42, "top_set_count": 24, "diverse_set_count": 24 } total_input is the total number of designs across run_ids before filtering; passing_filters is how many passed every hard filter; top_set_count is min(budget, total_input) (an upper bound, not necessarily reachable); diverse_set_count is the actual number of designs selected into the set, which SavedSet.design_count reports afterwards ( not total_input ). GET /api/saved-sets/{id}/designs returns every ranked design (pass or fail) with an in_diverse_set boolean; use this to browse the full ranked pool, and use SavedSet.design_count and total_input from GET /api/saved-sets/{id} for summary counts. SavedSet.source_run_ids lists the run IDs a set was built from; resolve them to display names via GET /api/runs . Run ingestion ¶ Used by the Select Runs UI to discover and persist runs from RUN_BASE_DIRS : GET /api/tree : browse allowed base directories. POST /api/runs/scan : body { "folders": ["/path/..."], "force_rescan_of_ingested": false } . Returns discovered run metadata; skips already-ingested runs unless forced. POST /api/runs/ingest-preview : body { "runs": [ ... ] } . Lists runs that would be re-ingested. POST /api/runs/ingest : body { "runs": [ ... ] } . Requires DATABASE . Assigns stable run_id , stores designs, and refreshes the cache. Only each run's path / merged_paths is read from the body: the server re-detects the run at those folders (which must be inside RUN_BASE_DIRS ) and stores what it finds on disk. A folder outside the base dirs, or with no recognised run, returns 400 . The server exits at startup if RUN_BASE_DIRS is empty or any entry is not an existing directory (except in desktop builds, which prompt for folders on first launch). Stored runs with folders or structure files outside the current RUN_BASE_DIRS are skipped at startup, logged as warnings, and left untouched in the database. Deleting a run ( DELETE /api/runs/{run_id} ) removes database and cache entries only; files on disk are unchanged. docs.text: Binderdash exposes a FastAPI REST API used by the Vue frontend and by scripts that analyse binder design runs. The same service also serves the built SPA and static assets. Pipeline outputs (BindCraft, RFdiffusion, RFdiffusion3, BoltzGen, and others recognised by run signatures ) are ingested into SQLite (or Postgres), cached in memory, and returned as JSON. Design rows include every column from the upstream results table plus Binderdash metadata. For machine-readable schemas, use the live OpenAPI document on your deployment. This page describes behaviour, authentication, and typical workflows.
docs.title: REST API

docs.text: Environment Typical base URL Your deployment https://binderdash.example.com Docker dev ( docker-compose.dev.yml ) http://localhost:8911 (host port mapped to container 8000 ) Local uvicorn http://localhost:8000 Resource Path Swagger UI /docs ReDoc /redoc OpenAPI JSON /openapi.json Health (no auth) /health (returns {"status": "healthy", "timestamp": "..."} ) Treat /openapi.json as authoritative for request and response shapes. The examples below cover common cases; new fields or routes may appear only in the spec.
docs.title: Base URL and OpenAPI

docs.text: Protected routes require credentials unless DISABLE_AUTHENTICATION=true (all endpoints public). Discover what is enabled: GET /api/auth/status Response includes auth_disabled and providers ( local , pam , google ) plus a top-level api_keys: {enabled, reason} ( reason is null , "auth_disabled" , or "persistence_disabled" ). Configure auth via .env (see .env.example ). Relevant variables: Variable Purpose DISABLE_AUTHENTICATION When true , skip all auth and CSRF checks LOCAL_USERS user:bcrypt_hash,... for POST /api/auth/login PAM_LOCAL_* Optional Unix PAM after local users PAM_GECOS_EMAIL When true , resolve a PAM user's email from the GECOS "other" (5th) field only GOOGLE_AUTH_* Optional Google OAuth SECRET_KEY JWT signing for session cookies BINDERDASH_ADMIN_USERS Comma-separated allowlist (email, provider:identifier , or bare username) granting admin; re-applied at every startup and login DATABASE Required for per-user API keys (stored in the database)
docs.title: Authentication

docs.text: API keys are per-user, named, expiring, and revocable ; there is no single shared server secret. Create one in the web UI (account menu, top-right > "API keys") or via CLI: python -m backend.cli user create --email you@example.org --admin python -m backend.cli key create you@example.org --name bootstrap The token is printed to stdout (a warning goes to stderr) and shown once: the server stores a SHA-256 hash instead of plaintext. Keys require DATABASE ; without persistence, key endpoints return 503 . Once you have a token, send it on every request, including POST / PATCH / DELETE . No session cookie or CSRF header is required. Supported headers (either is fine): Authorization: Bearer <token> X-Binderdash-Api-Key: <token> export BINDERDASH_TOKEN='<token from `key create`>' export BASE='https://binderdash.example.com' curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $BINDERDASH_TOKEN" "$BASE/api/runs" GET /api/auth/status reports api_keys.enabled: true when keys are usable (auth is enabled and DATABASE is configured). Invalid, expired, or missing keys receive 401 Authentication required . Manage keys via GET/POST /api/api-keys and PATCH/DELETE /api/api-keys/{id} using a browser session only. API-key requests to those routes receive 403 so a leaked key cannot create its own replacement. GET /api/users is admin-only and session-only. Do not commit keys to the repository.
docs.title: API key (scripts and automation)

docs.text: For interactive login (also required to create or manage API keys): POST /api/auth/login : body {"username": "...", "password": "..."} . Sets an HTTP-only session cookie and returns csrf_token and user . CSRF: state-changing methods ( POST , PUT , PATCH , DELETE ) must send header X-CSRF-Token matching the binderdash_csrf cookie. GET , HEAD , and OPTIONS are exempt. Missing or mismatched tokens return 403 with plain text CSRF token missing or CSRF token mismatch . POST /api/auth/logout : clears session and CSRF cookies. Google OAuth: GET /api/auth/google/login and GET /api/auth/google/callback (browser redirect flow). GET /api/auth/me returns the current user and requires a session cookie (API keys are not accepted; see backend/auth.py ). It returns username , provider , email , display_name , picture_url , user_id , is_admin , auth_method , and last_login_at . The login response ( POST /api/auth/login , and the Google callback) returns the same shape under user .
docs.title: Browser session (SPA)

docs.text: A user is a person; an identity is one login method, (provider, identifier) (for example, local:alice , google:alice@example.org , pam:alice ). Identities merge onto the same user only when they share a verified email , and users are created automatically on first login. BINDERDASH_ADMIN_USERS (comma-separated; matches email, provider:identifier , or bare username, with no * wildcard) grants is_admin and is re-applied at every startup and login, so admin status set only via the CLI ( user set-admin ) is overwritten unless the user is also listed there.

docs.text: One row from the run’s results table, plus Binderdash fields. Each design is a flat JSON object : all upstream table columns are copied in, so column names depend on the pipeline (e.g. BindCraft Average_i_pTM , RFD3 iptm , rf3_ipsae_min ). Common Binderdash fields: Field Description design_id Primary identifier from results table backbone_id design_id with MPNN / AF2 / BindCraft2 _candidate{n} and _seq{n} suffixes removed run_id , project_id , run_name , method , run_path Run context pdb_file Structure basename (not full path) source_path Distinguishes rows when runs are merged good User flag (boolean) tag "N" or "C" : terminus receiving preset tags in Prepare Sequences Sequence Binder amino-acid sequence (stored in extra_data ; extract / tag-placement) binder_chain Chain ID used for sequence extract (default B ) short_name Twist / vendor short identifier (≤32 chars) Persistence: Pipeline columns from the on-disk results table are stored in data_json and replaced on re-ingest. User annotations (uploaded table columns, extracted sequence, plugins) are stored in extra_data and preserved across re-ingest. The API returns a single flat dict: {**data_json, **extra_data} plus dedicated columns. The in-memory designs list is sorted by each method’s primary score (see table below). Client-side filtering and re-sorting are normal. Method Primary score columns (first match used) Default sort in cache bindcraft Average_i_pTM ascending rfd pae_interaction ascending boltzgen design_to_target_iptm descending rfd3 iptm , pair_pae , rf3_ipsae_min , rf3_rmsd_target_aligned_binder_rmsd_all descending rfd4_proteina oracle_ppi_iptm_coi , else consensus_z (refolded runs only) descending bindcraft2 i_pDAE (absent for a design with no interface contacts; those sort last) descending RFD4-Proteina's combined_scores.tsv carries only identity and sequence. Its scores are merged on ingest from the oracle's sibling table ( of3_inline_metrics.csv for OpenFold3, af3_inline_metrics.csv for AlphaFold3) in the same directory, joined per batch - example_id repeats across batches, so the key is the batch from dataset_name plus example_id . Merged columns have their dots flattened to underscores ( oracle_ppi.iptm_coi becomes oracle_ppi_iptm_coi ), generation hyperparameters and work-directory paths are dropped, and inline_metrics_oracle records which oracle produced them. The oracle reports pTM, ipTM and pLDDT on 0-100; these are rescaled to 0-1 on merge so they match every other method, while the PAE and RMSD columns stay in angstroms. _coi means the chain of interest, which for a binder run is the binder chain. BindCraft2 publishes structures per stage: accepted designs ( ranked.csv ) in results/bc2/ranked/ , refolded candidates ( refolded.csv ) in each batch's 2_Refolded/Complexes/ . A run detected on ranked.csv lists both, so pdb_count can exceed the design count. Note also that BindCraft2's bare pLDDT column is the binder chain's , not the complex average ( Target_pLDDT and Unbound_Binder_pLDDT are separate), which is what canonical binder_plddt resolves to. For BindCraft, ascending Average_i_pTM means lower values sort first in the API cache; re-sort client-side if “higher is better” for your analysis.

docs.text: POST /api/sequences/optimize-dna back-translates and optimises protein sequences using DnaChisel and python_codon_tables . Request body: { "sequences": { "design_id_1": "MAEK...", "design_id_2": "MGSS..." }, "codon_table_id": "e_coli_316407", "method": "match_codon_usage", "constraints": [ { "type": "EnforceGCContent", "enabled": true, "params": { "mini": 0.25, "maxi": 0.64 } } ], "fixed": { "design_id_1": [false, false, false, true] }, "frame": { "design_id_1": 0 } } Optional fixed maps each design_id to a per-residue boolean array the same length as that protein. Residues marked true must be stops ( * , frozen as TAA ) or a leading Met ( M , frozen as ATG ), and are excluded from codon optimisation and from user constraints. When a design id is omitted from fixed (or fixed is omitted entirely), every * in that protein is treated as fixed. Each result row includes the seed that produced its DNA, and the response includes tool_versions (DnaChisel, python_codon_tables, numpy). Passing those seeds back as seeds: { design_id: 12345 } reproduces the same DNA while package versions match (a DnaChisel upgrade can change the search order for a given seed). Omitting seeds assigns a new random seed per design, allowing retries to succeed when a strict constraint set fails. Lowercase a / c / g / t in a sequence are literal nucleotides from a custom addition, not amino acids: they stay frozen and are not recoded. Optional frame maps each design_id to 0 , 1 or 2 , the nucleotide offset where design and preset-tag codons begin. A 5' addition with a length not divisible by 3 sets this to 1 or 2. AvoidConsecutiveCodons reads codons from that offset.

docs.text: POST /api/sequences/prepare builds constructs (N/C tags, linkers, terminal prefixes and suffixes, start methionine, stop codons, post-stop padding, vendor short names, and protein parameters) from a design selection and a settings payload, returning the prepared rows and per-row warnings. The settings payload uses the same JSON format stored in a Prepare Sequences download bundle, so a saved bundle can be replayed. An invalid payload returns validation_errors instead of rows. POST /api/sequences/prepare/script returns a standalone Python script ( text/x-python ) that reproduces those constructs offline. The server generates it by inlining backend/seq_prep/ alongside a CONFIG block containing your settings, keeping the script matched to the server version. The script runs under uv run via a PEP 723 header, reads a TSV of designs with a tag column, outputs Twist CSV by default ( --format for FASTA/TSV/CSV/JSON), and embeds no sequences, hashes, or seeds so you can reuse it on later sets. This endpoint uses POST because the settings payload is a full JSON document.

docs.text: Each constraint: { "type": "<name>", "enabled": true, "params": { ... } } . Type Parameters EnforceGCContent mini , maxi (0–1); optional window for local GC AvoidHairpins stem_size , hairpin_window (exact Watson-Crick stems only) AvoidPattern pattern : literal string, RepeatedKmerPattern , or "EnzymeName_site" (e.g. "BsaI_site" ) AvoidRareCodons min_frequency ; species injected from codon_table_id UniquifyAllKmers k (e.g. 12) AvoidInvertedRepeats min_tm (°C, default 68); optional stride (default 10) AvoidConsecutiveCodons codons (default CGG , CGA , CCC ), max_run (default 2). Runs are counted in the design/tag frame ( frame on the request), not from nucleotide 0 EnforceTranslation is always applied by the server; do not send it. The Prepare Sequences UI uses DEFAULT_TWIST_CONSTRAINTS in frontend/src/stores/seqPrep.ts , similar to the DNA optimisation/complexity rules used by Twist Biosciences for gene synthesis. The UI-only type ExcludeRestrictionSite with params.enzyme is serialised to AvoidPattern with pattern: "<enzyme>_site" before POST. AvoidInvertedRepeats rejects sequences with self-complementary structures (snapback hairpins) melting at or above min_tm , computed the same way primer3 and IDT do (concentration-free nearest-neighbour thermodynamic alignment). This detects the short GC-rich and imperfect inverted repeats that gene-synthesis vendors flag and that AvoidHairpins (exact stems only) misses. primer3's alignment scores at most 60 bp per sequence, so hairpins are scored on sliding 60 bp windows; structures spanning more than ~50 nt (long arms and loop) may not be detected.

docs.text: { "results": [ { "design_id": "d1", "optimized_dna": "ATG...", "error": null, "seed": 847392011 }, { "design_id": "d2", "optimized_dna": null, "error": "Constraints could not be resolved (No solution found).", "seed": null } ], "elapsed_seconds": 2.31, "tool_versions": { "dnachisel": "3.2.16", "numpy": "2.3.2", "python_codon_tables": "0.1.18" } } Failures are reported per design. Because DnaChisel's constraint search is stochastic, any design failing with "No solution found" is retried from the same starting sequence up to five times with a new seed each time before returning that error; the reported seed is from the succeeding attempt. All other errors return immediately. If many rows still fail, relax UniquifyAllKmers or windowed EnforceGCContent first.

docs.text: Run scope for every /api/filtering/* call is an explicit run_ids list; there is no server-side "currently selected" state. How the Filtering tab uses these stages, including the BoltzGen-style weighted ranking, is described in Filtering and ranking . The pipeline has three independent stages, each individually reachable: Hard filters ( FilterSpec ): { "column": "...", "operator": "...", "threshold": <number|null>, "text_value": <string|null> } . column accepts a canonical metric name (see backend/filtering/metrics.py , e.g. iptm , rmsd , pae_interaction ) resolved per-method, a raw column name, one of the identity columns design_id / project_id / run_name / method / Sequence , or the user columns good and tag . Numeric operators < , <= , > , >= take threshold ; string operators contains , not_contains , starts_with , ends_with , equals , not_equals , regex take text_value ; is_empty / is_not_empty take neither. good is a three-state rating: equals with text_value "true" (good) or "false" (bad), or is_empty (unrated). tag is text ( N / C , or empty). Both columns are listed even when no design has a value yet; a missing column is treated as all null. Ranking ( RankingMetric ): { "column": "...", "weight": 1.0, "higher_is_better": true } , plus ranking_mode . worst_rank (the default when omitted, keeping older clients on boltzgen Algorithm 2) scales each design's rank on every metric by 1/weight and takes the worst (max) scaled rank. simple sorts lexicographically: more filters passed first, then the metrics in list order, ignoring weight . In both modes, num_filters_passed is included in the sort and failing designs are not dropped ; ranked always covers every input design. The Filtering tab sends simple by default. Diversity selection ( select_diverse ): lazy-greedy selection over binder sequence similarity + quality_score , controlled by budget (final set size), alpha (0 = quality only, 1 = diversity only), and optional size_buckets ( {"min", "max", "num_designs"} , capping selections per sequence-length range). Only designs that passed every hard filter are eligible : a design failing a filter cannot appear in the diverse or saved set, regardless of how small passing_filters is relative to budget . best_mpnn_only (default false) first keeps one design per backbone_id (best primary score; designs with no backbone are kept) so the budget is not spent on MPNN variants of the same backbone. It applies only when diversity selection runs. POST /api/filtering/run accepts a FilteringRunRequest body: name , run_ids , filters , metrics , budget (default 24), alpha (default 0, quality only; BoltzGen uses 0.001 for proteins and 0.01 for its peptide-anything protocol), size_buckets , random_state , apply_diversity (default true; when false, the saved set includes every design that passed the hard filters and budget / alpha are ignored for selection), and best_mpnn_only (default false; see stage 3). POST /api/filtering/diversity accepts the same selection fields without persisting a set. Response: { "saved_set_id": "...", "name": "...", "total_input": 10000, "passing_filters": 42, "top_set_count": 24, "diverse_set_count": 24 } total_input is the total number of designs across run_ids before filtering; passing_filters is how many passed every hard filter; top_set_count is min(budget, total_input) (an upper bound, not necessarily reachable); diverse_set_count is the actual number of designs selected into the set, which SavedSet.design_count reports afterwards ( not total_input ). GET /api/saved-sets/{id}/designs returns every ranked design (pass or fail) with an in_diverse_set boolean; use this to browse the full ranked pool, and use SavedSet.design_count and total_input from GET /api/saved-sets/{id} for summary counts. SavedSet.source_run_ids lists the run IDs a set was built from; resolve them to display names via GET /api/runs .
docs.title: Filtering, ranking, and diversity selection

docs.text: Used by the Select Runs UI to discover and persist runs from RUN_BASE_DIRS : GET /api/tree : browse allowed base directories. POST /api/runs/scan : body { "folders": ["/path/..."], "force_rescan_of_ingested": false } . Returns discovered run metadata; skips already-ingested runs unless forced. POST /api/runs/ingest-preview : body { "runs": [ ... ] } . Lists runs that would be re-ingested. POST /api/runs/ingest : body { "runs": [ ... ] } . Requires DATABASE . Assigns stable run_id , stores designs, and refreshes the cache. Only each run's path / merged_paths is read from the body: the server re-detects the run at those folders (which must be inside RUN_BASE_DIRS ) and stores what it finds on disk. A folder outside the base dirs, or with no recognised run, returns 400 . The server exits at startup if RUN_BASE_DIRS is empty or any entry is not an existing directory (except in desktop builds, which prompt for folders on first launch). Stored runs with folders or structure files outside the current RUN_BASE_DIRS are skipped at startup, logged as warnings, and left untouched in the database. Deleting a run ( DELETE /api/runs/{run_id} ) removes database and cache entries only; files on disk are unchanged.

docs.text: Download bundles ¶ A design bundle is a single zip archive containing downloaded design data and the UI state that produced it. You can inspect which runs, filters, ranking settings, and tags generated a folder of PDBs and sequences months later, and restore that state if the runs are still available. Three endpoints build bundles through backend/bundles/ : Entry point Endpoint Designs tab download button POST /api/bundles/designs Prepare Sequences download button POST /api/bundles/prepare-sequences Saved Sets "download" GET /api/saved-sets/{id}/download Call POST /api/bundles/estimate beforehand to get counts and byte sizes without reading structure files, allowing the UI to warn before a large download. Scope ¶ A bundle includes the rows currently in the Designs table : the selected designs if any are checked, or all filtered designs otherwise. It does not include unselected or filtered-out designs from the active runs. Contents ¶ All files are placed inside a single top-level folder matching the zip filename: the order name for Prepare Sequences, saved_set_<name> for a Saved Set, or binderdash_designs for a plain Designs-tab download. Extracting the archive creates that folder instead of unpacking files into the current directory. <order_or_set_name>/ manifest.json build info, file inventory with sha256, coverage counts designs.tsv one row per design, every column Binderdash holds binders.fasta binder sequences, >design_id binderdash_session.json the UI state that produced the bundle target_contacts.tsv cached per-residue distances and SASA (if computed) target_contacts_reference.json per-run apo SASA reference and compute parameters structures/rank0001_<run>_<name>.pdb schemas/*.schema.json JSON Schema for each JSON member README.txt Prepare Sequences adds constructs.tsv , constructs_aa.fasta , constructs_dna.fasta , constructs_twist_aa.csv , constructs_twist_dna.csv , and prepare_sequences.json . Every entry point writes the same core member list. A saved set created before UI state recording was added still includes binderdash_session.json , with "captured": false and a note explaining why it is empty. General tables use TSV only; the Designs tab still offers a separate CSV download, so duplicating rows in both delimiters inside the archive is unnecessary. constructs_twist_aa.csv and constructs_twist_dna.csv use CSV because they are Twist vendor upload formats (amino acid and nucleotide). If no optimised DNA is available, constructs_twist_dna.csv is omitted and a warning is added to the manifest. Cached target contacts ¶ target_contacts.tsv exports only records already present in binderdash_target_contacts_cache for the bundled designs. Computing SASA takes minutes, so downloads do not trigger it. Designs missing a cached record are listed in manifest.json under coverage.designs_without_contacts , alongside coverage.contact_params_key (records cached under an older parameter key are not readable by the current configuration and are excluded from coverage counts). sasa_apo is read from the per-run reference map, except when a run's target moves between designs; in that case the per-design record provides its own sasa_apo value and overrides the shared reference so the SASA delta stays accurate. Versioning ¶ Every JSON member includes schema_version , a kind discriminator, and the app version and git commit that generated it. Increment the major version only for breaking changes (removing or retyping a field); increment the minor version for additive optional fields. Readers reject any major version higher than the one they support and ignore unknown keys. backend/bundles/json_schemas.py generates schemas from the Pydantic models at request time so each schema matches its corresponding JSON data. To detect unversioned model changes, backend/tests/test_bundle_schemas.py compares each generated schema against a golden snapshot in backend/tests/fixtures/bundle_schemas/ . When that test fails, check whether the change is additive (regenerate the golden snapshot and increment the minor version) or breaking (add a new golden file, increment the major version, and keep the previous snapshot). SessionState and PrepareSequencesPayload use extra="allow" because they mirror Pinia stores that change independently of the backend, and rejecting a download with HTTP 422 over an extra pass-through frontend field would break exports unnecessarily. Presentational fields (coloured segment spans, display duplicates) are accepted on input and stripped before writing so the archive stores data only. Build identity ¶ backend/version.py resolves the app version and commit in this order: The BINDERDASH_GIT_COMMIT environment variable (set as a Docker build arg). backend/_build_info.json (written by desktop/packaging/build-common.sh for PyInstaller builds that have no .git directory). git rev-parse in a source checkout. unknown . Resolution is lazy and cached, so the git subprocess runs at most once per process and only when a bundle is built. Memory and size ¶ Bundles are written to a tempfile.SpooledTemporaryFile (up to 32 MB in RAM before spilling to disk) and streamed with an accurate Content-Length header. A streaming generator writer would omit Content-Length , turn mid-archive errors into truncated HTTP 200 responses, and still use similar memory because structure files are streamed in both approaches. Set BUNDLE_SPOOL_DIR for desktop deployments where /tmp is mounted on tmpfs (RAM), so spilled files write to disk instead of memory. docs.text: A design bundle is a single zip archive containing downloaded design data and the UI state that produced it. You can inspect which runs, filters, ranking settings, and tags generated a folder of PDBs and sequences months later, and restore that state if the runs are still available. Three endpoints build bundles through backend/bundles/ : Entry point Endpoint Designs tab download button POST /api/bundles/designs Prepare Sequences download button POST /api/bundles/prepare-sequences Saved Sets "download" GET /api/saved-sets/{id}/download Call POST /api/bundles/estimate beforehand to get counts and byte sizes without reading structure files, allowing the UI to warn before a large download.

docs.text: MCP server ¶ Binderdash exposes a Model Context Protocol server so an AI agent can analyse binder design campaigns directly: filtering and ranking designs, selecting diverse panels, inspecting interfaces, and saving curated Saved Sets for review in the web UI. The server uses stateless streamable-HTTP and is mounted in the same FastAPI process as the REST API at /api/mcp/ (note the trailing slash; POST /api/mcp returns a 307 redirect to it). Running in-process lets the MCP server share the REST API's in-memory design cache directly. Installing ¶ Docker (dev and production compose) enables MCP by default. backend/Dockerfile compiles with --extra mcp , so images built from it install fastmcp and mount /api/mcp/ . Both docker-compose.yml and docker-compose.dev.yml use that Dockerfile. Because Compose does not rebuild automatically after a Dockerfile change, run docker compose up -d --build once on an existing stack to pick it up. In a local virtual environment, fastmcp is an optional extra. Without it, the app starts normally without mounting the MCP endpoint (logged at INFO level on startup). To enable it locally: uv pip install -r backend/requirements.txt uv pip install "fastmcp>=3.4,<4" # or: uv pip install -e "backend[mcp]" The desktop build excludes MCP. PyInstaller installs from the checked-in backend/requirements.txt , which omits the mcp extra. Do not regenerate requirements.txt with --extra mcp . fastmcp pulls roughly thirty transitive packages ( keyring , jeepney / SecretStorage , aiofile / caio , and others) that load backends via entry points and D-Bus and are not listed in desktop/binderdash.spec 's hiddenimports . Containers do not have this PyInstaller constraint, so Docker enables the extra at build time. No environment variable toggles the mount; availability depends solely on whether fastmcp can be imported. Because the mount happens at module import time (before tests can patch settings), an environment flag would be untestable and could hide why the endpoint is absent. Authenticating ¶ MCP uses the same per-user API keys as scripted REST access (see Authentication ). Create one with: python -m backend.cli key create alice --name mcp Send it as Authorization: Bearer bd_… (canonical) or X-Binderdash-Api-Key: bd_… . Keys use the same TTL cache as REST, so revoking a key applies to both immediately. API keys require DATABASE . Without database persistence, no key store exists and all requests return 401 (logged as a startup warning). With DISABLE_AUTHENTICATION=true , the server mounts without authentication and logs a warning. Client configuration ¶ The web UI generates client snippets for you: open account menu > API keys > Create , then expand "Use with Claude Code or another AI agent (MCP)" or "Use Claude Science" on the new-key panel. Both prefill this server's URL and the new key. These sections appear only when MCP is mounted ( GET /api/auth/status reports mcp.enabled ). Add the server to Claude Code with one command: claude mcp add --transport http --scope user binderdash \ https://binderdash.example.org/api/mcp/ \ --header "Authorization: Bearer bd_your_key_here" Alternatively, edit ~/.claude.json (all projects) or .mcp.json (one project) directly. That command writes the following JSON structure, which other MCP clients also accept: { "mcpServers": { "binderdash": { "type": "http", "url": "https://binderdash.example.org/api/mcp/", "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer bd_your_key_here" } } } } The key is stored in plain text in that file, so use a dedicated expiring key per agent and revoke it from the UI when finished. A project-scoped .mcp.json is shared with anyone who clones the repository, and Claude Code prompts each user to approve the server before first use. For Claude Science, open Settings > Connectors > Add Connector , choose Local URL , and enter: Name: binderdash Server address: https://binderdash.example.org/api/mcp/ Type: Streamable HTTP Advanced settings: leave OAuth Client ID, OAuth Server URL, and Scopes empty, and paste the following into the header command field (Claude Science executes it locally on each connect and sends the printed JSON as request headers): echo '{"Authorization": "Bearer bd_your_key_here"}' The key is embedded in that command in plain text. The new-key panel's Use Claude Science section prefills these values. Tools ¶ Tool Purpose list_runs Projects, runs, methods, design counts , filters, timestamps, signed download URLs, merge groups describe_methods Canonical metrics, sort directions , ranking presets describe_columns Columns for a selection, per-method coverage and ranges query_designs Filter, sort, page and project the design table summarize_designs Quantiles and histograms without returning rows rank_designs Multi-metric rank-based scoring with a filter cascade select_diverse_designs Filter, rank, and de-duplicate by sequence; optional Saved Set saved_sets List, read, create (from design keys), rename Saved Sets extract_sequences Extract sequences from structures into the derived cache inspect_structures Chains, roles, sequences, binderdash_* interface metrics, and a tokenised structure URL read_structure_file Raw structure text, size-capped. Over the cap, the error includes a download URL export_structures Manifest plus an absolute GET URL for a tar of the structures list_target_residues Targets in a run scope, residue labels to filter on, contact coverage target_contact_profile Per-residue mean ΔSASA / closest approach / contact frequency prepare_sequences Add N/C tags, linkers, stops and short names; return a download URL for the ordering table merge_design_columns Add TSV/CSV columns to the design table (same as Upload extra data) No plotting tool is exposed: query_designs returns column-selected tabular data for an agent to chart itself. For bulk exports, list_runs provides designs_json_url and designs_tsv_url per run with a short-lived download_token (JWT claims bound to that run_id and format, valid for ~10 minutes). Fetch those URLs with curl without the MCP API key instead of raising query_designs limits past the response size cap. Download URLs are absolute when the server knows its public origin ( PUBLIC_BASE_URL , falling back to https:// plus DOMAIN , then the incoming request). The response also includes base_url . Each run reports ingested_at (first Binderdash ingest) and folder_mtime (run-directory mtime at ingest). inspect_structures returns one absolute structure_url per design with a token scoped to that run and filename. export_structures stashes the file list and returns an absolute GET /api/pdbs/tar?download_id=&download_token= URL that you can fetch with curl without an API key or request body. Both tokens expire after about 10 minutes, and the archive stash is cleared on server restart. read_structure_file enforces a size cap (20 KB default, 200 KB hard limit); exceeding the cap returns an error containing the download URL for local parsing. The structure_url field on rows from query_designs , rank_designs , select_diverse_designs , and saved_sets has no token and cannot be fetched directly; call inspect_structures or export_structures instead. Target contacts ¶ query_designs , rank_designs , and select_diverse_designs accept an optional target_contact_groups parameter alongside filters . A contact condition applies a threshold on a target residue (for example, "A166 within 5 Å of the binder (heavy atoms)" or "the epitope buries at least 30% of its surface on binding"), evaluated from the design's structure as a hard filter. {"target_key": "…", "label": "PD-L1", "filters": [ {"residues": ["A54", "A56"], "scope": "any", "metric": "distance", "distance_type": "heavy", "operator": "<=", "value": 5.0} ]} metric is distance (with distance_type ca , cb , or heavy ), sasa_bound , or delta_sasa . unit is angstrom or percent of the residue's theoretical maximum (Tien et al. 2013). scope is any or all of the listed residues, count (with min_count ), or site_percent (the metric summed over the listed residues). Supplying one group per target lets a single call specify equivalent residues under different construct numbering schemes; if a design's run is outside a group's scope, that group does not filter it. Call list_target_residues first to get the target_key and residue labels, and target_contact_profile to inspect which residues binders contact before choosing filter thresholds. Runs are grouped into targets by sequence (not chain ID), so one target spans runs that assign different chain letters. Computing per-residue contact records is not exposed as an MCP tool because parsing every structure in a selection takes minutes; trigger it from the Compute button in the web UI's Filtering tab. A design without cached contact records fails every contact condition, so tools emit a TARGET_CONTACTS_UNAVAILABLE warning and note in empty results that contacts may not have been computed yet. Preparing sequences for ordering ¶ prepare_sequences runs the same construct builder as the Prepare Sequences tab ( backend/seq_prep/ ): N/C-terminal tags and linkers, start methionine, stop codons, post-stop padding, and short names. Pass a run/design selection, a config matching the tab's settings, and format ( twist default, fasta , tsv , csv , or json ). prepare_sequences does not run DnaChisel, because constraint solving for a few hundred designs takes minutes and exceeds typical tool call timeouts. When DNA output is enabled, the tool returns an unoptimised reverse translation (matching the UI before you click Optimize DNA) with dna_optimized: false and a warning, because a plain reverse translation looks identical to optimised DNA on inspection and synthesis problems appear only after ordering. Generate constraint-checked DNA from the UI or its exported script. Construct rows are omitted from the tool response to avoid filling the agent context window. Instead, the response returns counts, warnings, and a download_url with a short-lived token scoped to that request and format (fetchable without the MCP API key). The server stores the request in memory without writing to disk and renders the file when you fetch the URL; the URL expires after the TTL or a server restart. Designs without a placed tag are skipped and reported in a skip list, so an unconfigured selection is flagged explicitly instead of outputting untagged constructs. Pass default_tag to supply a fallback terminus for untagged designs. The MCP write scope covers read and analysis operations, Saved Sets (including creating sets from design lists), merging extra TSV/CSV columns into designs, and compute-and-cache operations (sequence extraction, structural metrics) that populate derived caches. Scanning, ingesting, deleting, and cache refresh are not exposed. Differences from the REST API ¶ The MCP layer does not mirror the REST API; it addresses the issues catalogued in BINDERDASH_API_OVERHAUL.md without breaking existing REST clients: Sort directions are explicit: iptm and ptm are higher-is-better, while pae_interaction and rmsd are lower-is-better. order="auto" applies the expected direction, and requesting the opposite emits a SORT_DIRECTION_OVERRIDE warning instead of returning a reversed ranking without notice. Canonical column names resolve per method (for example, iptm maps to Average_i_pTM for BindCraft and design_to_target_iptm for BoltzGen). Canonical resolution takes precedence over a matching raw column name because pae_interaction is also RFdiffusion's raw column name, and matching the raw name first would leave other methods null. Server filesystem paths are omitted: pdb_file is replaced by structure_filename , structure_format , and structure_url ; params , target_sequence , run_path , and per-replicate ^\d+_ columns are excluded. Sorting, limit , offset , and column projection run server-side (REST does not support these). Errors and partial results are reported explicitly: a ranking metric that resolves for no design raises an error instead of being skipped, and a diverse set smaller than its budget explains why. Oversized responses return a RESPONSE_TOO_LARGE error instead of truncating output. Response shape ¶ Data-returning tools share one envelope. Rows are returned as arrays instead of objects (using 40-55% fewer tokens on wide tables) and floats are rounded to four significant figures: { "columns": ["run_id", "design_id", "method", "iptm", "structure_filename"], "rows": [["bc", "d1", "bindcraft", 0.9123, "d1.pdb"]], "total_matching": 1240, "returned": 25, "offset": 0, "truncated": true, "methods": {"bindcraft": {"columns": ["Average_i_pTM"], "higher_is_better": true}}, "warnings": [{"code": "MERGED_RUN", "message": "..."}] } Errors are formatted as [CODE] message and end with a concrete next tool call: UNKNOWN_COLUMN (including the nearest column names), AMBIGUOUS_DESIGN_REF , NO_RANKABLE_METRICS , RESPONSE_TOO_LARGE , EMPTY_SELECTION , SEQUENCES_REQUIRED , and INVALID_TARGET_CONTACT_FILTER . Implementation notes ¶ The package directory is backend/mcp_server/ (not mcp ), because pytest adds backend/ to sys.path , where a package named mcp would shadow the SDK imported by fastmcp . server.py : FastMCP instance, TokenVerifier , the ASGI app, the X-Binderdash-Api-Key header shim, and run_blocking (service-layer calls run in asyncio.to_thread , with a semaphore on heavy calls so an agent loop cannot starve the interactive web UI sharing the process). vocab.py : canonical metrics, sort directions, and ranking presets (moved server-side from frontend/src/config/rankingPresets.ts ). columns.py , refs.py , tables.py , errors.py , descriptions.py : shared column resolution, reference parsing, table formatting, error helpers, and tool descriptions. contacts.py : shared target-contact filtering. Conditions are evaluated into boolean __tc_* columns via filtering.service.build_filter_inputs (the same entry point used by the REST filtering endpoints) and appended to the hard filters, so tools treat them as standard filters and strip the virtual columns before returning rows. tools/ : discovery.py , designs.py , selection.py , structures.py , target_contacts.py . Two integration points in backend/main.py are required: CSRF exemption for /api/mcp/ : the MCP sub-app authenticates via Authorization only and does not read cookies, so CSRF protection does not apply. Without the exemption, a missing API key returns a text/plain 403 "CSRF token missing" response that MCP clients cannot parse. Lifespan chaining: mounting a sub-app in Starlette does not start its lifespan, which is where the streamable-HTTP session manager initializes. Without chaining the sub-app lifespan, imports succeed but every tool call fails at runtime with "Task group is not initialized" . Tool descriptions in descriptions.py are the agent's only documentation; treat edits to them as behaviour changes.

The MCP write scope covers read and analysis operations, Saved Sets (including creating sets from design lists), merging extra TSV/CSV columns into designs, and compute-and-cache operations (sequence extraction, structural metrics) that populate derived caches. Scanning, ingesting, deleting, and cache refresh are not exposed.

docs.text: The MCP layer does not mirror the REST API; it addresses the issues catalogued in BINDERDASH_API_OVERHAUL.md without breaking existing REST clients: Sort directions are explicit: iptm and ptm are higher-is-better, while pae_interaction and rmsd are lower-is-better. order="auto" applies the expected direction, and requesting the opposite emits a SORT_DIRECTION_OVERRIDE warning instead of returning a reversed ranking without notice. Canonical column names resolve per method (for example, iptm maps to Average_i_pTM for BindCraft and design_to_target_iptm for BoltzGen). Canonical resolution takes precedence over a matching raw column name because pae_interaction is also RFdiffusion's raw column name, and matching the raw name first would leave other methods null. Server filesystem paths are omitted: pdb_file is replaced by structure_filename , structure_format , and structure_url ; params , target_sequence , run_path , and per-replicate ^\d+_ columns are excluded. Sorting, limit , offset , and column projection run server-side (REST does not support these). Errors and partial results are reported explicitly: a ranking metric that resolves for no design raises an error instead of being skipped, and a diverse set smaller than its budget explains why. Oversized responses return a RESPONSE_TOO_LARGE error instead of truncating output.

docs.text: Data-returning tools share one envelope. Rows are returned as arrays instead of objects (using 40-55% fewer tokens on wide tables) and floats are rounded to four significant figures: { "columns": ["run_id", "design_id", "method", "iptm", "structure_filename"], "rows": [["bc", "d1", "bindcraft", 0.9123, "d1.pdb"]], "total_matching": 1240, "returned": 25, "offset": 0, "truncated": true, "methods": {"bindcraft": {"columns": ["Average_i_pTM"], "higher_is_better": true}}, "warnings": [{"code": "MERGED_RUN", "message": "..."}] } Errors are formatted as [CODE] message and end with a concrete next tool call: UNKNOWN_COLUMN (including the nearest column names), AMBIGUOUS_DESIGN_REF , NO_RANKABLE_METRICS , RESPONSE_TOO_LARGE , EMPTY_SELECTION , SEQUENCES_REQUIRED , and INVALID_TARGET_CONTACT_FILTER .

docs.text: The package directory is backend/mcp_server/ (not mcp ), because pytest adds backend/ to sys.path , where a package named mcp would shadow the SDK imported by fastmcp . server.py : FastMCP instance, TokenVerifier , the ASGI app, the X-Binderdash-Api-Key header shim, and run_blocking (service-layer calls run in asyncio.to_thread , with a semaphore on heavy calls so an agent loop cannot starve the interactive web UI sharing the process). vocab.py : canonical metrics, sort directions, and ranking presets (moved server-side from frontend/src/config/rankingPresets.ts ). columns.py , refs.py , tables.py , errors.py , descriptions.py : shared column resolution, reference parsing, table formatting, error helpers, and tool descriptions. contacts.py : shared target-contact filtering. Conditions are evaluated into boolean __tc_* columns via filtering.service.build_filter_inputs (the same entry point used by the REST filtering endpoints) and appended to the hard filters, so tools treat them as standard filters and strip the virtual columns before returning rows. tools/ : discovery.py , designs.py , selection.py , structures.py , target_contacts.py . Two integration points in backend/main.py are required: CSRF exemption for /api/mcp/ : the MCP sub-app authenticates via Authorization only and does not read cookies, so CSRF protection does not apply. Without the exemption, a missing API key returns a text/plain 403 "CSRF token missing" response that MCP clients cannot parse. Lifespan chaining: mounting a sub-app in Starlette does not start its lifespan, which is where the streamable-HTTP session manager initializes. Without chaining the sub-app lifespan, imports succeed but every tool call fails at runtime with "Task group is not initialized" . Tool descriptions in descriptions.py are the agent's only documentation; treat edits to them as behaviour changes.
